articles.title: Before the White House, Jimmy Carter was a Georgia farm boy who worked before dawn; his childhood farm is now a historic park
articles.summary: US News: Well before he took office as the 39th president of the United States, Jimmy Carter spent many years on a Georgia farm, where mornings were usually be.
articles.body: Well before he took office as the 39th president of the United States, Jimmy Carter spent many years on a Georgia farm, where mornings were usually before the break of dawn. Carter grew up in the small community of Archery, close to Plains, where he participated in activities such as planting, tending animals and undertaking chores that are characteristic of the rural environment. According to the National Park Service, today, the Jimmy Carter Boyhood Farm forms part of Jimmy Carter National Historical Park, where the landscape and buildings of his childhood are preserved. The site offers visitors a glimpse into the rural world that shaped Carter before his political career began.How did Jimmy Carter grow up on the Georgia farmCarter moved to his family’s farm in Archery at age four and lived there until he left for college in 1941. His father, Earl Carter, farmed cotton, peanuts, corn and sugar cane, while the family maintained a garden and raised livestock. Jimmy became accustomed to farm work from an early age, helping with crops, animals and household responsibilities. His days could begin before daylight, when he joined other workers to feed animals and prepare for the day’s labour. The farm had no electricity until 1938, meaning much of the family’s routine depended on manual work and daylight. Those years gave Carter an early understanding of agriculture, responsibility and rural community life.What kind of work did young Jimmy Carter do?Farm chores occupied a significant part of Carter’s childhood. He helped hoe fields, pick cotton, stack peanuts and care for livestock, learning practical skills through everyday work. He also found ways to earn money. As a young boy, Carter sold boiled peanuts in Plains, sometimes waking early on Saturdays before completing farm work and walking along the railroad tracks into town. Other chores included gathering eggs, carrying water, collecting firewood and tending animals. The work was demanding, but it also gave him practical knowledge of farming and the rhythms of rural life. Carter’s childhood was therefore shaped not by an occasional connection to agriculture, but by daily participation in it.When did the farm become part of the National Historical Park?The Carter family farm eventually became a protected historic landscape. The National Park Service acquired part of the original property, and the Boyhood Farm became an integral part of Jimmy Carter National Historical Park in 2000. Restoration work recreated the appearance of the farm before electricity was installed in 1938, helping visitors understand the conditions in which Carter grew up. Crops associated with the family’s agricultural life, including peanuts, cotton, corn and sugar cane, continue to feature at the site. Farm animals and historic buildings further reinforce the connection between the preserved landscape and Carter’s childhood. Rather than simply displaying a presidential birthplace, the park recreates the working environment that shaped him.Why is Jimmy Carter’s boyhood farm still being preserved today?The farm represents a side of Carter’s life that existed decades before he entered politics. Its preservation keeps alive the agricultural landscape, working routines and community surroundings that influenced his understanding of responsibility and stewardship. The park’s story is also continuing under new leadership. In a July 24, 2026 announcement, the National Park Service credited Karen Barry as the new superintendent of Jimmy Carter National Historical Park, noting her more than two decades of experience and her role in major preservation milestones, including the rehabilitation and opening of Carter’s Boyhood Home. The announcement described the park as moving towards preserving a legacy for future generations, ensuring that the places that shaped Carter remain accessible.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: US News: The creators of the hit animated series South Park have announced a tongue-in-cheek name change, renaming the long-running show as “South America” in .
articles.body: The creators of the hit animated series South Park have announced a tongue-in-cheek name change, renaming the long-running show as “South America” in an apparent dig at US President Donald Trump’s recent efforts to rename geographic landmarks.According to BBC and CNN, co-creators Matt Stone and Trey Parker announced the rebrand with a statement saying it was “inspired by the bravery and patriotism of Apple and Google”, referring to the tech giants adopting Trump’s preferred names for some geographic features on their US-based map services.The announcement came shortly after Trump appeared to suggest renaming New Mexico as “New America” in a series of posts on social media.Days earlier, he had signed an executive order seeking to rename Lake Ontario as “Lake America”.Trump had previously ordered the Gulf of Mexico to be referred to as the “Gulf of America” in the US. Google and Apple subsequently adopted the new name for users of their US-based map services, while other countries continued to use the traditional name.Mocking the development, Stone and Parker said: “We especially want to thank our parent company Paramount – a Skydance Capitulation.”The satirical rebrand was announced as South Park, which debuted in 1997, entered its 29th season. The show has frequently targeted Trump and his administration, with the president and his supporters repeatedly criticising its portrayal of him.The announcement also followed the show's latest Emmy win for Outstanding Animated Program. The official South Park social media account subsequently shared an image depicting a fictionalised Trump holding an Emmy award.It remains unclear whether “South America” will be a permanent name change or simply part of the show's ongoing satire.The new season of South Park is scheduled to premiere on September 16 on Comedy Central, with episodes also available on Paramount+ in several markets.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2001, a British-Brazilian family began reclaiming abandoned cattle pasture;  840,000 trees later, 1,500 acres of Atlantic Forest have returned
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Discover how the Locke family has restored 1,500 acres of Brazil's Atlantic Forest by planting 840,000 trees, transforming degraded pasture into vibrant ecosystems over two decades.
articles.body: In a landscape once used for cattle pasture, young native trees are growing into a very different habitat. In the hills of Rio de Janeiro state, the Locke family has spent more than two decades restoring parts of the Atlantic Forest through the creation and expansion of the Guapiaçu Ecological Reserve, known as REGUA. What began as an effort to protect the forest on the family's land has grown into a long-running restoration effort across degraded pasture, wetlands and fragmented forest. The scale of the change is striking. According to the World Land Trust, REGUA has planted about 840,000 trees on degraded land, mostly former pasture, restoring about 607 hectares, or 1,500 acres, to forest. The restored areas also help reconnect isolated forest fragments.From family land to a growing forestAccording to REGUA, the organisation was formally established as an environmental organisation in 2001, although the idea behind it had developed several years earlier. Nicholas Locke, who was born and raised in the UK, returned to Brazil as a young man and became involved with the family property in Guapiaçu. He and his wife, Raquel, gradually shifted the focus of the property away from traditional agriculture and towards conservation.The family’s connection to the land dates back much further. Nicholas Locke’s great-grandfather acquired the former Fazenda do Carmo in 1907. Over the following decades, parts of the property were used for agriculture and livestock, while sections of the original forest remained. By the 1990s, the family had become increasingly concerned about protecting these remaining forest areas and restoring the surrounding landscape. When REGUA was established, its work went beyond protecting the forest that remained. The organisation also began acquiring degraded land and restoring it, with reforestation becoming one of its central activities, particularly in lowland areas where forests had been cleared for pasture.Wildlife returns as the forest growsThe transformation has taken years. Trees planted in former pasture first had to survive the difficult early stages of establishment, while natural regeneration gradually added to the developing vegetation. REGUA’s restoration programme aims to rebuild ecological connections between isolated forest fragments. As restored areas mature, they can fill gaps between existing forest patches and create a more connected landscape. The organisation has also restored wetlands and other degraded habitats, extending the work beyond tree planting.The results are becoming increasingly visible. The World Land Trust states that more than 220 bird species have been recorded at the preserve, while capybaras, caimans and wetland birds have returned to restored areas. The reserve has also carried out species reintroduction programmes, including the return of lowland tapirs to Rio de Janeiro state after an absence of roughly 100 years. Research published in Environmental and Sustainability Indicators has also found that areas of the Brazilian Atlantic Forest undergoing active reforestation showed patterns of tree and mammal diversity that could approach those found in naturally regenerating secondary forests. The researchers also found that greater tree diversity was associated with greater mammal diversity, highlighting the importance of diverse native plantings in forest restoration. This does not mean newly planted forest immediately becomes equivalent to mature forest. Recovery takes time, and restored areas can still differ from older forests in structure and biodiversity. But the findings show how carefully managed restoration can help degraded landscapes develop more complex ecological communities.Where restoration takes rootToday, REGUA extends far beyond the original family property. The organisation manages many thousands of hectares through land acquisition and partnerships, while its restoration work brings together local staff, scientists, volunteers, conservation organisations and international supporters. Its nursery remains central to this effort, producing a steady supply of native seedlings from seeds collected in surrounding forests and helping ensure that restoration remains rooted in the region’s native flora.For the Locke family, restoring the land is not simply about replacing trees that were lost. It is about recovering parts of a landscape shaped by generations of farming, grazing and forest clearance. The former pasture will take many years to develop the structure of mature Atlantic Forest, but the planted trees are already changing the landscape, creating vegetation and habitat where open pasture once dominated. Over time, those young plantings can become part of a larger forest system reconnecting areas of habitat across the region.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Make ground in Gaza tremble': Egypt warned Netanyahu of Hamas plans before October 7
articles.summary: Middle East News: Fresh details have emerged about warnings issued to Israel ahead of the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack, amid a report that Prime Minister Benjamin Neta.
articles.body: Fresh details have emerged about warnings issued to Israel ahead of the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack, amid a report that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was warned by the United Arab Emirates about plans for a major assault in the weeks leading up to the invasion.The latest information also sheds further light on previously reported warnings from Egyptian intelligence officials during the same period.According to Army Radio, the Shin Bet intelligence service conveyed to Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu warnings from its Egyptian counterparts that Hamas intended to “make the ground in Gaza tremble.”The Egyptian side provided only a general warning, without offering any specific details.In the days following the October 7 onslaught, an Egyptian intelligence official said Jerusalem had ignored repeated warnings that the Gaza-based terror group was planning “something big,” including an apparent direct warning from Cairo’s intelligence minister to Netanyahu, as cited by Times of Israel.According to the report, then-Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar assessed that the warning referred, at least in part, to Hamas seeking to raise the issue of kidnapped Israeli researcher Elizabeth Tsurkov in talks with Israel over a potential hostage deal.Shortly before the warning was issued, Hamas and Iraqi Shiite militia Kataeb Hezbollah, the group holding Tsurkov, had reportedly agreed that she would be treated as a Hamas asset in negotiations with Israel.The talks would involve the release of a large number of terrorists in exchange for the handover of two Israeli captives and the bodies of two IDF soldiers held in Gaza.The development comes as a new investigative report by Israeli newspaper Haaretz claimed that UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed had warned Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that then-Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar was preparing a “major attack” against Israel. Netanyahu, however, reportedly did not share the warning with Israel’s senior security leadership.Around 10 days after their reported conversation, Hamas launched its October 7, 2023, attack on Israel.The Haaretz report is based on the new book Kidnapped: 843 Days of Abandonment, which claims that bin Zayed spoke to Netanyahu for 45 minutes from Abu Dhabi. During the conversation, bin Zayed also reportedly urged Netanyahu to address broader sources of instability, including Gaza’s economic situation and rising tensions in the West Bank.According to a UAE presidential adviser interviewed for the book, bin Zayed was “surprised” by Netanyahu’s response, saying the Israeli prime minister did not appear “alarmed”.However, Netanyahu's office has rejected the claims made by the report.In a post on X, the Israeli Prime Minister’s Office said that any exchange of relevant information between the two countries took place solely through intelligence channels.“The press reports are false. No warning was given to the Prime Minister by the United Arab Emirates before October 7. If there was any relevant information, it was passed through intelligence channels between the two countries,” it posted.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: US Streamers News: A social media post has reignited a sharp dispute surrounding Candace Owens and Erika Kirk, with Natalie Jean Beisner accusing Owens of using language.
articles.body: A social media post has reignited a sharp dispute surrounding Candace Owens and Erika Kirk, with Natalie Jean Beisner accusing Owens of using language that she believes crosses a line. The post, shared on September 9, focuses on Owens' remarks about Kirk and questions the way the controversy has been presented to the public. It has quickly drawn attention to the increasingly heated tone surrounding the debate.Natalie Jean Beisner calls out Candace Owens over Erika Kirk commentsThe post shows journalist Natalie Jean Beisner responding directly to comments attributed to Owens about Erika Kirk. Beisner argues that the language used against Kirk goes beyond political disagreement and could contribute to a hostile public atmosphere.Her post specifically highlights Owens' description of Kirk's connections and role, while also accusing Owens of repeatedly presenting Kirk in a dehumanizing way.Beisner wrote:“Candace Owens to Erika Kirk: “You work with the deep-state apparatus. You are their emotional asset.”Candace once again weaponizes dehumanizing language against Erika Kirk.This is how political violence comes to happen and to—perhaps worse yet—be excused and even celebrated. Candace has repeatedly and intentionally and sinsterly conditioned her audience to think of Erika as less than and something other than human. She is playing a dangerous game”The post reflects a wider argument over where political criticism ends and personal attacks begin. Beisner's central concern is not simply the disagreement between Owens and Kirk, but the potential impact of repeated rhetoric on an audience.That distinction matters because political personalities often have large platforms capable of shaping how supporters view opponents. Strong criticism can attract attention, but accusations that someone is being portrayed as less than human can trigger an entirely different debate.Candace Owens controversy draws questions over New York Times articleThe accompanying discussion also moves beyond Owens' comments about Kirk and turns toward a broader criticism of how recent developments have been covered.The speaker questions why a particular piece appeared in The New York Times and why readers were required to access it through a paywall. The criticism then shifts toward the perceived transformation of Turning Point and the way its current direction is being described.The full comment said:"Always same perspective that he held somehow immediately. That was something she reversed course on and felt comfortable having them in her home. Okay, fine.So right off the bat, we're just going, why is this in the New York times? Why is it behind a paywall? And why can't you just do anything that feels normal? And as Charlie was, I guess you've been honest, it's just turning point 2.0. It has nothing to do with turning point 1.0. It's a totally different organization. It's unattainable. You work with the department of war. You work with the deep state apparatus. You are their emotional asset. We get it.It just feels like you're laying it on thick. And like, maybe you could have just published a sub stack here that if I'm running your PRH to a sub stack about how you feel, don't put it behind a paywall. What you've learned about grief."The exchange illustrates how quickly one controversy can expand into a larger fight over media coverage, political organizations and public messaging. For now, Beisner's post puts the focus squarely on the language being used in the dispute involving Owens and Kirk, while the wider conversation continues to grow online.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Singaporean man pleads guilty in $245m crypto theft in US; blew millions on jets, supercars, clubs
articles.summary: US News: A 22-year-old Singaporean, Malone Lam, pleads guilty in a federal court for participating in a $245 million cryptocurrency theft and laundering scheme, showcasing an extravagant lifestyle funded by crypto crime.
articles.body: A 22-year-old Singaporean man has admitted helping run an international scheme that stole and laundered more than $245 million in cryptocurrency through social engineering.Malone Lam, who had been living in Miami, pleaded guilty Tuesday in federal court in Washington, DC, to one count of participating in a racketeering conspiracy, US Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro announced.Prosecutors said Lam helped organise the operation, selecting victims and assigning roles to other members of the network. The group allegedly used information obtained through deception, along with occasional break-ins at victims' homes, to gain access to cryptocurrency wallets.The conspiracy began no later than October 2023 and continued until at least May 2025, according to court documents. Investigators said participants were based across several US states as well as overseas, with some connections formed through online gaming platforms.Lam used several aliases, including "Anne Hathaway", "$$$" and "King Greavy", according to prosecutors.The stolen cryptocurrency was used to fund an extravagant lifestyle, including private jet travel, luxury watches worth more than $500,000, designer clothing and handbags, and rental properties in Los Angeles, the Hamptons, and Miami.Prosecutors also said members of the group spent as much as $500,000 on nightclub services in a single evening, handed out expensive handbags at parties and maintained private security. The enterprise also acquired exotic cars valued from $100,000 to $3.8 million.Lam was arrested on September 18, last year at a rental property in Miami.Attorney Pirro said investigators would continue pursuing those involved in the operation."If you build a cybercrime empire, we will find you, dismantle your operation, and hold you accountable," he said.Lam entered his plea before US District Judge Colleen Kollar-Kotelly, who scheduled his next status hearing for December 8.The investigation involves the US Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia, the FBI's Washington Field Office, and the IRS Criminal Investigation Washington, DC, Field Office, with support from federal offices in California, Florida, and New Jersey.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Samsung phone stops working in 2 months; company told to pay Rs 37,499
articles.summary: News News: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Kerala has directed Samsung and three others to refund Rs 22,499 to a customer after finding deficiency i.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Kerala has directed Samsung and three others to refund Rs 22,499 to a customer after finding deficiency in service over failure to provide effective warranty service for a mobile phone that stopped working within two months of purchase. The commission also awarded Rs 10,000 for mental agony and Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs. The order was passed on August 31, 2026.Why did the customer approach the commission?According to the commission order, the customer purchased a Samsung Galaxy A15 5G mobile phone for Rs 22,499 on February 8, 2025, along with a compatible charger for Rs 1,399. The phone came with a one-year warranty.The customer said the phone suddenly stopped functioning on April 6, 2025, and did not respond even when the power button was pressed or when it was connected to a charger.He alleged that when he approached the dealer and an authorised Samsung service centre in Pathanamthitta, they directed him to another service centre in Kottayam, where he was told that the phone had a board-related problem and that repair would cost about Rs 10,000.The complainant further claimed that despite the phone being within the warranty period, he was asked to pay for the repair. When he refused, he was also allegedly asked to pay service charges for taking back the unrepaired phone. The phone was eventually returned without repair.The customer, who said he was a school teacher and also conducted online tuition classes, told the commission that he used the phone to record tutorial videos and conduct online classes. He claimed that he had to arrange another phone and suffered financial loss, inconvenience and mental agony.Samsung opposed the complaint, saying liquid had entered the phone and that salt traces and rust were found inside the handset. It claimed this amounted to mishandling and was therefore excluded from warranty coverage.What did the commission find about the warranty dispute?The bench comprising President George Baby and member Nishad Thankappan noted that the phone had become completely non-functional within about two months of purchase and that it was covered by a one-year warranty.The commission said Samsung had not produced independent technical material to establish that the damage was caused by the customer's actions or that the warranty exclusion applied.“When a manufacturer seeks to deny warranty service on the ground that the defect falls within an exclusion clause of the warranty, the manufacturer must establish the factual basis for such exclusion,” the commission held.It noted that Samsung had referred to liquid ingress, salt traces and rust, but had not produced a technical report, expert report, photographs, job card or other convincing evidence to establish the alleged damage or show that it was caused by the customer.“The mere assertion that liquid traces and rust were found inside the handset, without producing reliable technical evidence demonstrating the nature and cause of the alleged damage, cannot by itself be treated as sufficient proof of consumer mishandling, particularly when the device became defective within about two months of purchase,” the commission said.The commission also noted that the other service centres had not appeared before it or filed any response explaining their conduct. It found that the customer had been denied effective warranty service even though the phone became non-functional during the warranty period.“Nevertheless, the complainant is entitled to warranty protection unless the opposite party establishes a valid exclusion. Accordingly, this Commission finds deficiency in service on the part of the opposite parties in failing to provide effective warranty service to the complainant,” it held.The commission said the customer was entitled to a refund of the phone's purchase price as considerable time had passed without effective warranty repair. It partly allowed the complaint and directed all four opposite parties to jointly and severally pay Rs 22,499 to the customer against return of the defective phone.The commission also awarded Rs 10,000 for mental agony, inconvenience and harassment and Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs. The amounts have to be paid within 30 days of receipt of the judgment. If the refund and compensation are not paid within that period, they will carry 9 percent annual interest from the expiry of the 30-day period until realization.

articles.title: Blackouts, fuel shortages and empty taps: How Cuba’s energy crisis is disrupting daily life
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Cuba is facing a growing crisis as long power cuts, fuel shortages and lack of water make daily life harder for millions of people. The crisis is also.
articles.body: Cuba is facing a growing crisis as long power cuts, fuel shortages and lack of water make daily life harder for millions of people. The crisis is also taking a toll on people's mental health, with many struggling to see when conditions will improve.According to The Associated Press, blackouts in Cuba are now lasting more than 24 hours in some areas. The power cuts have also affected water supplies, transport and phone services, adding to the problems faced by ordinary people.“Before there was hope. Right now, what people have lost is exactly that,” Dr Yomeidis Felicó Riverón, a primary-care doctor, told AP. She said some patients come to her simply to cry and talk about their problems.The electricity crisis is at the centre of Cuba's problems. The country's power system is struggling with a lack of fuel, leading to longer and more frequent blackouts. The outages also affect water systems because many depend on electricity to pump and distribute water.Water shortages have become a serious problem in several parts of Cuba. The US Embassy in Havana has warned that the country's water system is becoming increasingly unstable, with some areas going for long periods without public water.The situation is also creating health risks. The US embassy has warned of an increase in stomach illnesses linked to problems with water and energy supplies, including cases involving E. coli, norovirus and Shigella.US energy pressure on CubaThe worsening crisis comes as the United States increases pressure on Cuba's energy supplies. In January 2026, US President Donald Trump ordered measures against countries that provide oil to Cuba. His administration said the move was aimed at putting pressure on the Cuban government.The US also imposed new sanctions on September 3 against Cuba's Oil Industry Supply Import Company, known as Abapet. The company imports equipment and spare parts used to maintain Cuba's power grid.The latest US measures are part of a much longer dispute between Washington and Havana.Relations between the two countries changed sharply after Fidel Castro's 1959 revolution in Cuba. Castro's government moved closer to the Soviet Union, while the United States began imposing economic restrictions on Cuba.The US later introduced a broad trade embargo that remains in place today. Relations improved under former President Barack Obama, who restored diplomatic ties with Cuba in 2015 and eased some restrictions.However, former President Donald Trump reversed many of those steps during his first term. The Biden administration made some limited changes, but the wider US embargo remained.Trump's return to office has brought another sharp increase in pressure on Cuba, with energy supplies now a major focus of the US campaign.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: South Australia sank a 40-metre dredger six kilometres off Adelaide; the ship now rests 20 metres underwater as a new reef in a $165 million algal-bloom recovery plan
articles.summary: Rest of World News: South Australia has sunk the 40-metre MV Andrew Wilson about six kilometres off the coast of Brighton, turning the retired vessel into an artificial r.
articles.body: South Australia has sunk the 40-metre MV Andrew Wilson about six kilometres off the coast of Brighton, turning the retired vessel into an artificial reef. The ship now rests upright 20 metres below the surface on the sandy ocean floor.According to the govt of South Australia, the sinking is part of the $165 million response to the algal bloom that affected marine life in the area. The artificial reef is intended to support the recovery of fish and other marine life after the impact of the algal bloom.The MV Andrew Wilson made its final journey this week after travelling about 40 kilometres from Port Adelaide to Brighton. It was anchored overnight before specialist crews began the operation to sink it. Valves were opened to allow seawater into the hull, causing the vessel to gradually sink and settle on the seabed.The operation also marks the first time in more than 20 years that a vessel has been scuttled in South Australian waters. Before the wreck can be opened for recreational diving, teams will carry out a final safety inspection in the coming days.Ship to become artificial reefOnce the site is opened, divers will be able to explore parts of the vessel, including its engine room, galley and bridge. The location was selected because it is accessible, has suitable seabed conditions and is close to boat ramps. It is also at a safe distance from major shipping channels.The wreck is expected to become another part of wider efforts to help restore marine biodiversity in the area. The state government said the project builds on other recovery work, including the construction of native oyster reefs and restoration of seagrass habitat.An artificial reef provides a structure in an area where there may otherwise be little solid habitat. The submerged ship will add a large surface under the water where marine life can establish itself. Fish and other organisms can use such structures as part of the marine environment.However, the ship could not simply be placed in the water in its original condition. Preparing the vessel for scuttling was a detailed process that began several months ago after Maritime Constructions donated it to the State Government.Specialist crews removed hazardous materials from the vessel before it was sunk. They also removed internal walls and cut strategic access holes into the hull. A deep clean was carried out in consultation with the Environment Protection Authority and an independent specialist.The government said the preparation followed strict international guidelines to prevent negative impacts on the local marine environment. This ensured the vessel was prepared specifically for its new role beneath the water.Fishing banned around wreckThe government has also introduced a temporary fishing restriction around the new reef. Recreational and commercial fishing is banned within a 200-metre radius of the ship for 12 months.The restriction is intended to give local fish stocks time to thrive around the new artificial reef. The species mentioned by the government include snapper, flathead and King George whiting.South Australia’s Department of Primary Industries and Regions lists the MV Andrew Wilson site among areas where all fishing activity is prohibited during closure periods. Fishing closures can be permanent, seasonal or temporary, and are used to reduce fishing pressure and help replenish fish numbers.For the new reef, the 12-month closure is temporary. It creates a protected area around the wreck while the site begins to develop as part of the surrounding marine environment.The MV Andrew Wilson was built in 1962 and has a long history in South Australian waters. During its working life, the vessel carried out local dredging operations and supported earlier artificial reef installations. It also played a role in the salvage mission following the Whyalla Airlines tragedy in May 2000.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Indian-origin couple donates $20 million to US university to set up AI, advanced analytics college; institute to be named after them
articles.summary: US News: Anuradha and Vikas Sinha have pledged $20 million to the University of North Texas for the creation of a new college focused on artificial intelligence and advanced analytics, aimed at enhancing educational and research opportunities in AI.
articles.body: Indian-origin couple Anuradha and Vikas Sinha have donated $20 million to the University of North Texas to expand education and research in artificial intelligence and advanced analytics, according to the university’s press release.The university will name its new Anuradha and Vikas Sinha College of Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Analytics in recognition of the gift, creating an academic centre focused on developing and using AI and intelligent systems.The donation will fund six permanent endowments covering college leadership, scholarships, professorships, entrepreneurship and incubation, advanced research and emerging technologies.The new college will bring together programmes in areas including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, data science, health informatics, information science, library science and learning technologies. It will also connect researchers and students across disciplines through shared infrastructure, research projects and industry partnerships.Vikas Sinha, who earned his PhD in information science from UNT in 2023, said the couple wanted the investment to expand what students can do with AI."Artificial intelligence will be one of the defining technologies of our generation, and universities have an essential role to play in preparing the people who will shape its future," he said.The college is expected to have two academic divisions. One will focus on developing and deploying intelligent systems, while the other will examine how information and intelligent systems operate in human and institutional settings.UNT will also establish an Applied Artificial Intelligence and Data Science Institute to link AI and analytics research and education across the university, with a focus on interdisciplinary research, external funding and industry collaboration.The Sinhas moved to the US after completing bachelor's degrees in civil engineering at Sri Venkateswara University. They later earned graduate degrees from Florida Atlantic University.Vikas Sinha subsequently studied at Northwestern University before completing his doctorate at UNT. He is now vice president of the Mainframe Software Division at Broadcom and has served on the UNT College of Information Leadership Board since 2023.The couple has previously supported UNT's data science programmes. In 2024, they helped establish the Anuradha and Vikas Sinha Department of Data Science, followed by a major gift in 2025 that created the Sinha Innovation Lab for Data Science.Sinha said his experience as an international student influenced the couple's decision to support education."Education has opened doors for us throughout our lives, and we want to hold those doors open for others," he said."For us, this gift is about paying that opportunity forward and recognising that immigrants don't simply participate in the American dream, they help build it."UNT President Harrison Keller said the new college would help the university respond to the rapid changes brought by AI in work and research.The University of North Texas is a public research university in Denton, north of Dallas, and was founded in 1890.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
